__doc__: Maintained by session-start-prep.py + session-end-flush.py + check-iteration-trigger.py + user-prompt-inject.py + maintenance_workorder.py (all writes go through _state_io's lock/atomic-replace/three-way-merge). Drives dormant/wake-up detection, memory decay gating, pending_maintenance state, summary drift repair history. The dormant profile itself lives only in .workframe-config.json (dormant_profile); a dormant_profile key left here by older versions is no longer read. last_prompt_injected_session_id: session id ("sid:<id>", or the session counter when no id is available) whose first prompt already carried the maintenance reminder (latest only, kept for compatibility); prompt_reminded_sessions (written on demand) keeps the last 200 such markers so interleaved sessions do not take each other's first prompt (a bound, not a guarantee: after 200 other sessions an old session's next prompt counts as first again); on upgrade the single legacy marker is folded into it. maintenance_notified (written on demand): version keys (<PM id>#<content digest>) of maintenance items already shown once; an item is shown again only when its content changes. recent_drift_repairs (v0.2.2): ISO timestamps of recent SessionStart drift repairs in last 30d, read by /core:audit for the repair frequency. DEPRECATED: weighted_events_since_last_iteration is kept for backward compatibility only — nothing reads or updates it.

__pending_maintenance_schema__.__doc__: Field contract for each pending_maintenance entry. Written by check-iteration-trigger.py upsert_pending(); GC'd by session-start-prep.py after status=closed or retired + closed_at older than PM_CLOSED_RETENTION_DAYS. Kept here (not in prose docs) so the contract ships with the plugin and stays machine-checkable.
__pending_maintenance_schema__.kind: signal category: memory_backlog / close_check_due (entries of kinds no longer produced may linger as retired until they expire)
__pending_maintenance_schema__.dedup_key: stable identity WITHOUT a time component — a time-bearing key piles up synonymous entries while the condition stays unresolved
__pending_maintenance_schema__.status: open | closed | retired (session-start-prep.py: an open entry of a kind no longer produced; not a dismissal, never a baseline)
__pending_maintenance_schema__.closed_at: ISO-8601 or null. NOT just an audit stamp: for a closed entry this timestamp IS the baseline for the entry's own dedup_key — dismissing a signal means the user judged everything before that moment handled, so check-iteration-trigger.py restarts that kind from here (dismissal_baseline(); per dedup_key, closing one kind never affects the other). Two shapes: the evidence-filter kind (close_check_due) only counts stale entries whose last_marked_at is > closed_at; the suppression-window kind (memory_backlog) is skipped wholesale while a non-GC'd closed entry exists — it scans current notes state, so there is no evidence timestamp to compare and no separate constant to tune. Consequences: never hand-edit it — this entry is the only carrier of the suppression, so its GC deadline (PM_CLOSED_RETENTION_DAYS) is how long the suppression lasts.
